Take-home Exercise 1

Geospatial analytics for public safety

Option B examines road accidents recorded across the Bangkok Metropolitan Region in 2022. The report covers the six required tasks and adds a space-time analysis; the slide deck condenses the evidence for an executive audience.

NoteMain result

The final pattern contains 3,597 distinct recorded accidents. Broad concentration centres on Bangkok and extends towards Samut Prakan. The inhomogeneous L-function test still finds excess neighbouring events after the 319 repeated-coordinate events are removed. The bonus Knox test finds more space-time-close pairs than expected under time permutation.

Submission outputs

Technical report

The Quarto HTML report documents all six tasks, the data-quality decisions, first- and second-order analyses, sensitivity checks, bonus test, limitations and references.

Executive summary

The revealjs deck has a cover, contents page and nine content slides, within the stated limit.

GitHub repository

The repository contains the Quarto sources, analysis scripts and rendered website files.

Brief at a glance

The official exercise brief requires six connected tasks:

  1. Acquire, inspect, clean, validate, transform, and document the spatial data.
  2. Analyse first-order spatial and temporal intensity with justified parameters.
  3. Test second-order spatial structure against a stated null model.
  4. Integrate the first- and second-order evidence, including uncertainty and alternative explanations.
  5. Present readable statistical graphics and maps, with no more than 150 words for each major visualisation.
  6. Write public-safety implications in no more than 500 words, separating evidence from recommendations that need more information.

The bonus analysis must answer a useful geospatial question beyond the core requirements. A new package or decorative visualisation alone does not meet the bonus standard.

Selected study design

The analysis uses Option B: Thailand road accidents in 2022. Event records come from the Thailand Road Accident 2019-2022 dataset, while provincial boundaries come from geoBoundaries Thailand ADM1.

The Bangkok Metropolitan Region is operationalised as Bangkok, Samut Prakan, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Pathom, and Samut Sakhon. This six-province definition is documented by Thailand’s National Statistical Office. Distance and area calculations use WGS 84 / UTM zone 47N (EPSG:32647).

Analytical coverage

  • The data audit traces 81,735 raw records to 3,597 analysed events and documents missing coordinates, spatial filtering, province mismatches and duplicate handling.
  • First-order analysis compares monthly and hourly patterns, provincial event density and edge-corrected KDE at 2 km, 3 km and 6 km bandwidths.
  • Second-order analysis uses transformed L-functions, translation edge correction and 99 conditional simulations under CSR and an inhomogeneous Poisson model.
  • Sensitivity checks compare KDE bandwidths and repeat the inhomogeneous test after removing repeated coordinates.
  • The bonus applies a 199-run Monte Carlo Knox test at three space-time thresholds.
  • Fixed URLs, source-file checksums, scripts, parameters, a simulation seed and session information document the workflow.
